title: Gazipur workers block highways over Tk 17,000 wage; 300 factories suspend production
excerpt: Workers in Gazipur demanded Tk 30,000 a day after the wage board vote. BGMEA said 300 factories stopped work and about 100 used the "no work, no pay" rule.
content:
Garment workers blocked the Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways in Gazipur on Wednesday (25 November), hours after the Minimum Wage Board set the new entry-level wage at Tk 17,000, Prothom Alo reported. Workers said the rate was too low and repeated a demand for Tk 30,000.

Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Amzad Hossain told Prothom Alo that police fired tear gas in several places and that 20 factories declared holidays. Four factories in Sreepur upazila were vandalised that morning, the newspaper reported, and some put up notices of a three-day closure.

Mahmud Hasan Khan, president of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), told The Daily Star that violence in Ashulia, Savar and Gazipur forced 300 factories to suspend production on Wednesday, and that nearly 100 invoked the "no work, no pay" provision of Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act. He said many factories could struggle to pay the new wage, but all parties should accept it because every board member had signed the pay scale.

The board voted 4-2 for Tk 17,000, up 36% from Tk 12,500, as Devlens reported. Wages for grades one, two and three were set at Tk 21,500, Tk 20,000 and Tk 19,200. The rate still needs labour ministry approval and is due to take effect on 1 December, Prothom Alo reported. Babul Akhter, the workers' representative on the board, said "our expectation is not fulfilled" but that the industry could pay. Nazma Akter, president of Sommilito Garments Sramik Federation, said the decision must be respected and that buyers should help pay for it.

The Sammilito Garments Federation Oikya Parishad, a platform of several federations, backed the new structure at a press conference and urged workers to return to work, UNB reported. Its adviser, Humayun Kabir Khan, BNP assistant secretary for labour affairs, welcomed government plans for seven specialised hospitals in industrial areas offering free treatment, rice at Tk 30 a kg through Open Market Sales, and an appeal to landlords not to raise rents.

Why it matters

Closures under "no work, no pay" cut income in the weeks before the new rate starts. NGOs running workers' clinics, legal aid and childcare in Gazipur and Ashulia should expect pressure on household budgets and possible job losses at smaller factories.

What to watch

  • The labour ministry's gazette notice of the new wage, due before 1 December.
  • Whether protests continue and how many factories stay closed.
  • Delivery of the promised OMS rice and the rent appeal in industrial areas.
